name: Paseah
overview: Paseah is a male member of the tribe of Levi, known specifically as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant highlights his service in the religious duties associated with the worship and maintenance of the sanctuary, as recorded in Ezra 2:49.
namesAndTitles: The name Paseah means "hobbling one." This proper name, recorded in Ezra 2:49, does not appear to have been given by God but reflects a personal or familial designation within the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Paseah as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe responsible for temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Paseah's significance lies in his role as a temple servant from the tribe of Levi during the post-exilic period. His inclusion in the list of those returning to Jerusalem underlines the restoration of temple worship and the reestablishment of Levitical duties, emphasizing the continuity of God's ordained worship practices through faithful service.
